method: Single printed items split from the automatic families of 1788, and of 1787 where they reach the 1788 pages (long-running ones included), counted by machine over all 2,379 pages of 1788 in both transcriptions and joined into documents; the admitted and chosen items counted again by their own opening, and scan checks of each admitted passage, by the thin-year rule (Y-THIN, as amended with the owner's choice B1): eligible when printed by more than half of the papers that survive for the item's weeks and by at least 4; eligible items printed by every paper that survives for their weeks admitted; the others chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news
scan_scope: Each crop covers the excerpt, the opening of the printed item. Long documents were not proofread in full.

new_groups.label: A letter of the President of the late Federal Convention to a friend in Fredericksburg, Virginia, on his return from the Convention
new_groups.definition: Printings of an extract of a letter 'of a late date, from the illustrious President of the late Federal Convention, to his friend in Frederickburgh, Virginia', taken from Mr. Green's Virginia Herald: 'I thank you for your kind congratulation on my safe return from the Convention'; the writer gives his view of the Constitution the Convention proposed. The letter-writer's own words, as the papers printed them.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1788 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: The King of France's Council of State, 29 December 1787: an act for the encouragement of the commerce of France with the United States

Extract from the Records of the Council of State. The King, desirous of encouraging the commerce of his subjects with the United States of America'; it sets the duties and privileges on American goods in France. An act of the French government, printed after the letter with which a French official sent it.

new_groups.label: Congress, 13 September 1788: the days for appointing electors, for choosing the President and for beginning proceedings under the Constitution

new_groups.label: A letter from L'Orient of 17 July 1788 on troubles in France

dispositions_summary.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN, chosen by the owner on 23 November 2026 and amended the same night with the owner's choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; the eligible items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted (1 in 1788), and the others are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (a target, not a quota); one affair's items are handled as in X-1800-01; the eligible items not chosen are listed here.
dispositions_summary.paper_counting: 1788 has 7 catalogue series, which are 6 papers (C-04): the New-York Journal under two catalogue numbers (sn83030566, daily, to 26 July; sn83030567, weekly, from 31 July). The New-York Packet (5 issues) and the Independent Journal (2 issues) survive only in a few weeks, so 4 or 5 papers are in print in any three weeks and an item needs 4 papers all year.

dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1788 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json), and the families of 1787 were looked for on the 1788 pages (items_from_1787.json). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by machine by about 100 words of its text from the finder's position, over all 2,379 pages in both transcriptions (a dense run of its word 5-grams, at least a quarter of them); the counts were joined into documents (items standing together on most of the same pages). The news among the documents in 3 or more papers was counted again by about 70 words from its own opening (counts_1788.json), and the pages that print another text sharing the words were read and left out. Each admitted printing was checked against its page scan.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Counted by their own words and joined into documents, 13 items of 1788 are eligible: 13 in 4 papers, 0 in 5, 0 in 6. 1 item is printed by every paper that survives for its weeks and is admitted; 6 more are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news; together they are 7 of the eligible documents. 6 eligible items, all notices or advertisements, are not chosen and are listed with their counts. 8 more candidates counted by their opening are below the bar and listed. 108 more documents of the item finder are in 3 papers or fewer by their own words, below the bar (docs_1788.json); they are not listed one by one.
counted_item_by_item.Titles of the items not chosen: Each eligible item not chosen is a notice or an advertisement and is described, not quoted, so as not to name the private persons it names; each candidate below the bar is listed by a title of the review's.
